resources.scope: US guidance; do not assume US reporting channels or shortcodes apply in Sri Lanka.

source.title: FTC — How To Recognize and Avoid Phishing Scams
source.context: Use a website or number independently known to be real, not contact details in the message. If a link may have downloaded harmful software, update security software and scan.

actions.text: If you sent money, contact the bank, card issuer or payment service you actually used immediately through its trusted app or the number on your card. Report the suspected scam and ask whether the payment can be stopped or reversed; recovery is not guaranteed.

If you shared a password, change it through the service’s trusted app or independently reached website, change reused passwords, and enable two-factor authentication. If you shared an OTP, PIN or card/bank details, contact the relevant provider immediately through an independently trusted channel.

If you clicked, close the page and do not enter information, approve prompts or download anything. Clicking alone does not prove an account was compromised. If anything downloaded or installed, update trusted security software and run a scan.
Do not reply, follow the message’s links, call its numbers, or share codes or money. Check the claim using an app you already trust or contact details obtained independently of the message.

In Sri Lanka, keep the message and transaction references for your report, then use Sri Lanka CERT’s incident portal for scam-related assistance. Reporting does not replace contacting your payment provider urgently if money or banking details were involved.

limitations: Resources are reviewed offline, not live-verified. Organization relevance is not sender authentication or proof of fraud. Regional availability and reporting procedures can differ.
General contact and head-office numbers are not dedicated fraud hotlines. Contact the provider you actually used for payment, which may differ from the organization named in the message.
guidanceResources.fallback: If a reviewed resource is missing or outdated, use an official app you already trust, the number printed on your card or statement, or an official channel you independently obtained. Do not use contact details from the suspicious message or assume an old contact is current.
